riskFree.source: Frozen USD 10-year Treasury yield as of 2025-12-12 (4.2%).

beta.source: Beta of 1.56 from 104 weekly returns 2023-12-15 to 2025-12-12 against the S&P 500.

equityRiskPremium.source: Long-run U.S. equity risk premium of 5.0% (Damodaran-style implied ERP); no registered excerpt.

costOfDebt.source: Blended pre-tax cost of debt: recent senior notes coupons of 5.25%-6.17% (e3152b99f67) and TTM interest expense of $3.85B on $108.1B debt; 5.5% used.

taxRate.source: Normalized 15% cash tax rate; TTM effective rate is 11.2% (fact effective_tax_rate_ttm) and is expected to normalize with U.S. cloud build.

equityWeight.source: Reference close $189.97 x 2.873B shares = $545.8B equity value; debt $108.075B + finance leases $4.976B = $113.051B; equity weight 82.8%.

discountRate.rationale: WACC is built from a 4.2% risk-free rate, 1.56 beta and 5.0% ERP, giving about 12.0% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt is about 4.7% on a 5.5% pre-tax cost and 15% tax rate, weighted 82.8% equity / 17.2% debt. One rate is used for all scenarios; operating risk is reflected in cash flows, not in separate discount rates.

shares.rationale: No equity note or treasury-stock schedule was read in the frozen evidence, so no incremental dilution reserve is added. Reported diluted weighted shares of 2.922B are about 1.7% above basic and are treated as a sensitivity, not a separate reserve.

notes: Operating leases of $18.679B are treated as operating expense and excluded from debt claims; finance leases of $4.976B are included.
Debt claims = debt $108.075B + finance leases $4.976B + preferred $0 + minority interest $0.506B = $113.557B.
Net bridge = $93.791B, matching the registered valuation_net_claims fact.

bear.narrative: RPO is not guaranteed cash. The bear case assumes power, data-center and financing constraints delay or cancel large AI contracts, so revenue growth falls from 8% to 2% and operating margin drops to 26% as depreciation and underutilization bite. Capex is cut to $42B near term and $24B later. Terminal growth of 2% and ROIC equal to WACC mean no excess return at maturity. This is a coherent delayed-conversion path, not a fixed haircut to the base.
triggers: Large RPO contracts slip by more than 12 months or are cancelled
Cloud revenue growth falls below 20% in a quarter
Capex remains above $42B without matching revenue
Operating margin falls below 28%
invalidation: RPO conversion accelerates and cloud growth stays above 30%
Operating margin holds above 30% while capex falls
Free cash flow turns positive earlier than year 5

revenue.rationale: Long-dated RPO conversion slows and AI cloud demand is constrained by power and capital; revenue growth fades from 8% to 2%. RPO is treated as a schedule, not guaranteed cash.

margin.rationale: Underutilized capacity, depreciation from the build and pricing pressure compress operating margin to 26%, below the 30.3% TTM level; SBC remains expensed in margin.

capex.rationale: The build is cut to protect liquidity and funding: capex falls from $42B to $24B as delayed projects are deferred. TTM capex of $35.5B and 1H FY26 capex of $20.5B show the starting scale.

base.narrative: Oracle enters the forecast with $523B of RPO, up 438%, Q2 FY26 cloud revenue +34% and IaaS +68%, but TTM FCF is -$13.2B because capex is $35.5B versus $7.1B of D&A. Base assumes the RPO converts broadly on schedule but not linearly: revenue grows 18-20% early, then fades to 6% as the largest AI contracts anniversary. Capex peaks at $52B and falls to $32B; depreciation lags and rises through the horizon. Operating margin holds near 30% and expands to 33% as cloud scale and software mix offset depreciation and SBC. The terminal 3% growth and 12.5% ROIC are below the build-phase returns but above WACC, reflecting a mature cloud infrastructure business.
triggers: RPO conversion at or above schedule
Cloud revenue growth above 30% and IaaS above 50%
Capex peak no higher than $55B
Operating margin at or above 30% through the build
invalidation: RPO conversion slips by more than 12 months

revenue.rationale: Base revenue grows 18% in year 1, 20% in years 2-3 and fades to 6% by year 10, reflecting $523B RPO, Q2 cloud +34% and IaaS +68%; total revenue was +14%. The path assumes broadly on-schedule conversion, not a linear RPO burn.

margin.rationale: Base operating margin starts near 30%, around the 30.3% TTM level, dips as depreciation from the build ramps, then rises to 33% by scale and mix; SBC is expensed in operating margin.

capex.rationale: Base capex stays high at $46-52B through year 4, then declines to $32B as data-center build matures. TTM capex of $35.5B and 1H FY26 capex of $20.5B support a high but fading build.

bull.narrative: The bull case assumes the $523B RPO converts faster and Oracle wins incremental AI capacity contracts, so revenue grows 22-25% early and 7% at year 10. Scale, software mix and pricing lift operating margin to 35%, above TTM, as depreciation is absorbed and SBC growth slows. The bull case reinvests more than base, with capex of $52-62B early, so it is a faster-growth-and-more-capex path rather than a margin-only upside case. Terminal growth is 3% and ROIC is 15%.
triggers: RPO conversion accelerates and new AI contracts are signed
IaaS growth stays above 70% for multiple quarters
Operating margin reaches 33% before year 5
Capex is funded without straining the balance sheet

revenue.rationale: Bull revenue grows 22-25% early and 7% at year 10 as RPO conversion accelerates and Oracle wins incremental AI capacity business; Q2 IaaS +68% and RPO +438% show the demand is possible.

margin.rationale: Scale, software mix and pricing lift operating margin to 35%, above the 30.3% TTM level, as depreciation is absorbed and SBC growth slows; this is the explicit normalization basis for the above-history margin.

capex.rationale: Bull reinvests at least as much as base: capex is $52-62B early and still $36B at year 10, reflecting the extra data-center capacity required for faster RPO conversion.

lower.narrative: Lower normal case: ordinary demand and execution uncertainty slows RPO conversion but does not cancel it. Revenue grows 14-15% early and 5% at year 10; operating margin is 29-31%; capex is $44-47B early and $29B at year 10. Terminal growth is 2.75% and ROIC 11.5%, above WACC but below base.
triggers: RPO conversion slower by one or two quarters
Cloud growth in the high-20s rather than above 30%
Capex peak near $47B
Operating margin around 29-31%
invalidation: RPO conversion accelerates to base or bull pace

revenue.rationale: Lower normal revenue assumes slower but not cancelled RPO conversion, with 14-15% early growth fading to 5%; this is ordinary timing uncertainty around the $523B schedule.

margin.rationale: Lower normal margin assumes less cloud utilization and pricing, holding operating margin at 29-31% rather than the base expansion to 33%.

capex.rationale: Lower normal capex peaks near $47B and falls to $29B, reflecting ordinary build slippage rather than cancellation.

upper.narrative: Upper normal case: ordinary upside in RPO conversion and cloud share gains. Revenue grows 20-23% early and 7% at year 10; operating margin rises from 30.5% to 33.5%; capex is $50-58B early and $34B at year 10. Terminal growth is 3% and ROIC 14%. This is not the bull tail: it assumes solid execution and better scale, not a step-change in contract wins.
triggers: RPO conversion at or above schedule
IaaS growth above 60% for several quarters
Operating margin reaches 32% by year 5
Capex peak near $58B with matching revenue
invalidation: RPO conversion slips or cloud growth falls below 25%

revenue.rationale: Upper normal revenue assumes on-schedule RPO conversion and cloud share gains, with 20-23% early growth fading to 7%; Q2 cloud +34% and IaaS +68% support the demand side.

margin.rationale: Upper normal margin rises from 30.5% to 33.5% on cloud scale and software mix, above TTM but below the bull 35%; this is ordinary operating leverage, not a new pricing regime.

capex.rationale: Upper normal capex is $50-58B early and $34B at year 10, higher than base to support faster conversion but below bull's $62B peak.

fairValueBasis.rationale: The normal range is set by ordinary uncertainty in RPO conversion timing, cloud utilization, depreciation and capital spending, not by the bear/bull tails. Lower assumes slower conversion, 29-31% margins and $47B peak capex; upper assumes on-schedule conversion, 30.5-33.5% margins and $58B peak capex. Both use the same FCFF model, 10-year horizon, WACC, bridge, shares and method weights, with the base as the central case.

dcf.rationale: DCF is primary because ORCL is in a build phase: TTM capex is $35.5B versus $7.1B D&A and FCF is -$13.2B, so only a multi-year FCFF path captures the capex hump and the conversion of $523B RPO. Terminal value is sensitive to capex and margin, so DCF is weighted 60%, not more.

ev_ebitda_forward.rationale: Forward EV/EBITDA applies the peers' trailing median 19.3x to year-3 EBITDA and checks how the market prices scaled cloud growth after the build. It carries terminal economics but peers have different capex intensity, so weight is 25%.

pe_forward.rationale: Forward P/E applies the peers' trailing median 31.6x to year-3 core EPS and checks equity earnings after interest and tax. It is weighted 15% because EPS can be distorted by SBC and depreciation during the build.

bear.rationale: RPO concentration and capex/financing risk make a delayed-conversion path plausible; TTM FCF is negative and net debt is $112.5B.

base.rationale: Base is the central path: RPO supports strong growth but heavy capex delays free cash flow; Q2 cloud and IaaS momentum is real.

bull.rationale: Upside requires faster RPO conversion and margin scale; Q2 IaaS +68% and RPO +438% show it is possible but not assured.
